title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
authors: Tim Dettmers*, Artidoro Pagnoni*, Ari Holtzman, Luke Zettlemoyer (* equal contribution)

code.title: artidoro/qlora and bitsandbytes
code.note: the training script (qlora.py), the Guanaco scripts and every generation and GPT-4 and human judgment behind the chatbot results (eval/), MIT licence; the 4-bit kernels, NF4 and paged optimizers live in bitsandbytes (MIT), and the method ships in Hugging Face transformers and PEFT

takeaway: NF4 + double quantization + paged optimizers + all-layer LoRA over a frozen 4-bit base matches 16-bit finetuning quality, fitting 65B finetuning on one 48GB GPU (Guanaco: 99.3% of ChatGPT on Vicuna).
verdict: Believe the method: NF4 is the best of the 4-bit types tested (we reproduce the ordering on five small open models and the exact NF4 values from the code), the memory arithmetic holds, and the recipe has been the default way to finetune on one GPU since. Read the chatbot claims as rough: 99.3% of ChatGPT is a GPT-4 score on 80 prompts, its interval is about ±3, the Elo intervals of ±1 measure only the order of matches (resampling the prompts gives about ±40), and the 16-bit match is shown at 65B only against 16-bit LoRA, not full finetuning.

resources.t: Making LLMs even more accessible with bitsandbytes, 4-bit quantization and QLoRA
resources.by: Younes Belkada, Tim Dettmers, Artidoro Pagnoni, Sylvain Gugger, Sourab Mangrulkar (Hugging Face), 24 May 2023
resources.n: the canonical practitioner guide, co-written with the paper authors; covers NF4, double quantization and the transformers and PEFT API (BitsAndBytesConfig, load_in_4bit).
the best visual intuition for absmax and blockwise quantisation, NF4, and where QLoRA sits among GPTQ and AWQ style methods.

resources.t: Practical Tips for Finetuning LLMs Using LoRA
resources.n: hands-on hyperparameter guidance (r, alpha, target modules, memory trade-offs) that reflects the paper's adapters-on-all-layers finding, with a measured QLoRA memory and runtime trade-off.

resources.t: Finetuning LLMs with LoRA and QLoRA: Insights from Hundreds of Experiments
resources.n: empirical study of QLoRA's memory savings against runtime cost and quality across settings.

resources.t: NF4 Isn't Information Theoretically Optimal (and that's Good)
resources.n: a short note showing that absmax blocks change the distribution NF4 is built for, and the AF4 code it proposes (both are on the quantiser tab).

resources.t: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
resources.n: the systematic study of position, verbosity and self-enhancement bias in GPT-4 judges that QLoRA's §6.2 anticipated.

kb.t: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
kb.n: the adapter method QLoRA builds on, with a LoRA you can train in the browser; QLoRA's contribution is making the frozen base 4-bit and showing that all-layer adapters are needed at scale.

kb.t: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback (InstructGPT)

kb.t: ZeRO: Memory Optimizations Toward Training Trillion Parameter Models
kb.n: the bytes-per-parameter accounting (weights, gradients, optimizer states) behind the 780 GB of 16-bit finetuning.

kb.n: paging applied to the KV cache at serving time; QLoRA pages optimizer states during training.
